column4: The source section says the root ج-م-ع names both the attacked human جمع and the great gathering day; this ayah calls it a day when people are gathered and witnessed (مشهود). It makes the local crowd open onto the universal assembly, where presence itself marks the day.

The source section links a surprised crowd to humanity's final gathering; here people first surge into one another, then the trumpet is blown and they are gathered (فجمعناهم جمعا). The verse stages the scale change the section describes.

The source section's root ج-م-ع moves from a human crowd to the Day of Gathering; this ayah says God gathers people for يَوْمِ الْجَمْعِ and calls it the Day of mutual gain and loss. That name brings the crowd's gathering into the reckoning of what each person has gained or lost.

The source section turns from horses rushing into a small crowd to the resurrection gathering; here, after the trumpet, people stream from graves toward their Lord (ينسلون). Their urgent movement carries the raid's forward rush into the final assembly.

The source section says the great crowd is gathered on a day; here one cry is enough, and all are together and brought before God (جميع لدينا محضرون). It makes the universal gathering immediate and complete.

The source section scales a raided local crowd up to the day all people assemble; this ayah says God gathers them and leaves none behind (فلم نغادر منهم أحدا). It specifies the gathering's total reach.

The source section's gathering day places humanity before its Lord; following 18:47's gathering of everyone, this ayah shows them presented before the Lord in rows (صفا). The row itself adds an ordered public assembly to the prior verse's completeness.

The source section names the great day with the root ج-م-ع; this ayah warns of يَوْمِ الْجَمْعِ, when people are assembled and divided between the Garden and the Blaze. It joins gathering to the fates that make the assembly consequential.

The source section says the root ج-م-ع names the final gathering; the prayer here calls God جامع الناس for a day about which there is no doubt. It gives the crowd's gathering a universal and certain horizon.

The source section opens جَمْعًا from a battle crowd toward the final day; this ayah asks what it will be like when people are gathered for a doubtless day and each soul is repaid in full. The verse makes the assembly a setting for reckoning.

The source section connects the human جمع to the Day of Gathering; this ayah says God will surely gather people for the Day of Resurrection. Its direct root wording confirms that the crowd-word reaches the final assembly.

The source section contrasts a small attacked people with the gathering of all humanity; this ayah says God will surely assemble people for the Resurrection Day, with no doubt in it. It makes the final assembly the scale beyond any tribe.

The source section's root ج-م-ع names the final gathering; this ayah moves from God's giving life and causing death to His gathering people for the Resurrection Day. It connects the grave's return to the day on which all are brought together.

The source section lets the root ج-م-ع name a crowd and the day humanity is gathered; here the speaker says their Lord will gather them and judge between them in truth. It adds adjudication to the assembly.

The source section's local جمع opens toward all people gathered on the Last Day; this ayah describes the earth splitting and people rushing out, then calls that assembly an easy gathering for God (حشر علينا يسير). It supplies the grave-to-assembly scene.

The source section scales a crowd to the gathering of everyone; this ayah says God can gather the creatures He has dispersed through the heavens and earth whenever He wills (على جمعهم). It widens the image beyond a human encampment.

The source section's root ج-م-ع takes a human crowd toward the Last Day; this ayah says every one will be brought together before God (جميع لدينا محضرون). It stresses that no human stands outside the assembly.

The source section uses جَمْعًا for a crowd at the center of a raid; this ayah asks whether a human thinks God cannot collect his bones (نجمع عظامه) after death. It shifts collection from the whole crowd to the body's scattered parts.

The source section's جمع joins a small people to the day all are gathered; this ayah calls the Day of Decision the day God gathers the present audience and earlier peoples (جمعناكم والأولين). It makes the assembly span generations.

The source section pictures a crowd at the center of a raid and then humanity gathering; this ayah says people will come on the appointed day in groups (أفواجا). It supplies a direct image of the final multitude arriving in bands.

The source section moves from one attacked crowd to the gathering day; here the God-fearing are gathered to the Merciful as an honored delegation (وفدا). This is a specific, favorable form of the same mass movement.

The source section's final assembly brings the small crowd to a universal day; this neighboring verse drives criminals to Hell thirsty (ونسوق المجرمين). It sets the gathered crowd's punitive destination against the honored delegation in 19:85.

The source section says the Day of Gathering joins many people but the day reveals loss and gain; here the disbelievers are driven to Hell in groups (زمرا). It shows the assembled multitude sorted into a condemned company.
The source section's gathering day reaches all people; here the reverent are led to the Garden in groups (زمرا). Paired with 39:71, this gives the assembly distinct and opposite destinations.

The source section moves from a local crowd to the final day; this ayah shows every community kneeling and each community summoned to its record. It makes the gathered mass legible as accountable communities.

The source section says what lies in the breasts is collected for the day; after 45:28 summons each community to its record, this ayah says the record speaks the truth about what people did. The record supplies the evidence behind the assembly's accounting.

The source section's root ج-م-ع names the assembly, and its witness-root ش-ه-د names presence; this ayah says that on the day God gathers everyone, He asks the angels whether these people worshipped them. It makes the gathering a scene of testimony and questioning.

The source section joins gathering with witnessing; answering God's question in 34:40, the angels deny being worshipped and declare God their protector. Their answer completes the prior verse's scene of the gathered being confronted with testimony.

The source section's ج-م-ع moves from a human group toward the final assembly; this ayah says that when people are gathered, the beings they invoked become their enemies and deny their worship. The assembly reverses the alliance that formed the group.

The source section turns an attacked crowd into humanity gathered before God; here God gathers everyone and asks the idolaters where their claimed partners are. The assembled crowd faces the collapse of its former affiliations.

The source section scales a human crowd up to a universal gathering; this ayah gathers jinn and humans together and has the jinn acknowledge the people who followed them. It broadens the assembly and exposes the relation between its two groups.

The source section says ج-م-ع names the gathering of people; here God gathers everyone and separates the idolaters from their claimed partners. It gives the mass gathering a concrete scene of separation.

The source section's final day brings a crowd before its Lord; here all people appear before God together (برزوا لله جميعا), and the weak and proud argue. It shows a public assembly where the group's hierarchy is exposed.

The source section expands a local crowd into a final gathering; this ayah says the Lord will gather all people, with wisdom and knowledge. It connects the assembly's scale to the Lord's knowledge of those assembled.

The source section moves from a collective crowd to the day everyone is gathered; this ayah says each people will be called with its leader. It adds the way the universal assembly is addressed in identifiable communities.

The source section describes a great gathering after the trumpet; this ayah says the trumpet is blown and the criminals are gathered on that day, blue-eyed. It narrows the universal assembly to a marked group under judgment.

The source section's final gathering is the scale beyond a local human group; this ayah says God spread people through the earth and that they will be gathered to Him (تحشرون). It links dispersal across the world to assembly before God.

The source section lets the final day gather humanity; here God gathers those who worshipped and what they worshipped, then asks whether the worshippers misled them. The assembly becomes a confrontation between a group and its supposed leaders.

The source section's root ج-م-ع names a human crowd; here Pharaoh's people are summoned to assemble (مجتمعون) for the public contest. This is a worldly crowd gathered to watch a confrontation, a smaller counterpart to the final assembly.

The source section ties the final day to what is exposed about people; this ayah says God raises and gathers them all, where they swear to Him as they had sworn to people. It makes hidden duplicity visible in the universal gathering.

The source section scales a human crowd up to the gathering day; this ayah says God spread people through the earth and that they will be gathered to Him (تحشرون). It joins worldwide dispersion to return before God.

The source section treats gathering as humanity brought together before God; this ayah tells people to fear God, to whom they will be gathered (تحشرون). In its context of private conversations, it makes that future assembly a boundary on present speech.

The source section describes horses penetrating the middle of a human crowd; this ayah names the two hosts who met at Badr (التقى الجمعان), one fighting for God and one disbelieving. It gives the battle-crowd image a direct Qur'anic counterpart.

The source section's root ج-م-ع names a human battle crowd; this ayah calls the day the two groups met (التقى الجمعان) the Day of Decision. It joins the battlefield meeting of crowds to a decisive day.

The source section pictures a crowd caught by a raid; this ayah recalls the day the two groups met (التقى الجمعان) and says some turned away. It supplies the reversal of a crowd's cohesion under pressure.

The source section's crowd is a human group caught in battle; this ayah refers to the day the two groups met and says what befell them was by God's permission. It frames a battle crowd's fate as more than its visible force.

The source section's root ج-م-ع names the mass of people under attack; here believers are warned that people have gathered against them (جمعوا لكم). It depicts a crowd as a threat assembling before an encounter.

The source section stages charging horses as a force against a human crowd; this ayah commands preparation of war steeds to deter an enemy. It gives the horse's military force a defensive counterpart.

The source section's horses charge into a human group; here Satan is told to rally people with his cavalry and infantry (بخيلك ورجلك). The link is the specific image of mounted force mobilized with people, though this is a metaphorical command rather than a raid.

The source section reads the root و-س-ط spatially as the place between two sides; this ayah calls the community an أمة وسطا and immediately makes it a witness-community over humanity. Its distinct ethical sense links centrality to the section's other root ش-ه-د, while remaining different from the horses' position in a crowd.

The source section's root و-س-ط marks the center between the edges of a crowd; this ayah marks the middle prayer (الصلاة الوسطى) within the prayer sequence. The link is specifically central position, though here it orders prayers rather than people in space.

The source section's root و-س-ط means the place between two ends; this ayah uses أوسط for the ordinary, moderate measure of food fed to one's family. The relation is a measured middle rather than a crowd's spatial center, so it is a secondary lexical connection.

The source section's root و-س-ط places the horses between the crowd's two edges; this ayah calls one speaker أوسطهم among the garden owners, often read as their most balanced member. The link between a middle position and a voice within a group is plausible, though the sense is not spatial.

The source section's witness-root ش-ه-د describes being present; this ayah asks what it will be like when a witness is brought from every community and the Messenger is a witness over his people. It turns the gathered communities into witnesses and the witnessed.

The source section explains the root ش-ه-د through a gathering place and the act of being present; this ayah warns of the disbelievers' share in the scene of a tremendous day (مشهد يوم عظيم). It makes the Day itself a place of public appearance.

The source section's root ش-ه-د concerns witnessing; this ayah says that on the Day their tongues, hands, and feet testify against people about what they did. It specifies how the gathered person's conduct becomes public testimony.

The source section says the witness-root ش-ه-د is about being present; this ayah seals mouths on the Day and has hands speak while feet bear witness. It shows the body testifying in the accounting the gathering makes possible.

The source section says what was hidden in breasts is collected; here, when people reach the Fire, their hearing, eyes, and skins testify against them. It shows concealed deeds becoming evidence at the end-time reckoning.

The source section connects inner contents with testimony; after the body parts testify in 41:20, this ayah records the people asking their skins why they testified and the skins answering that God made them speak. It completes the prior verse's exposure scene.

The source section says what lies in breasts is collected on the final day; this ayah says people will be exposed and no secret of theirs will remain hidden. It states the disclosure that the collection of inner contents implies.

The source section explains the root ش-ه-د as gathering and presence; this oath pairs a witness with that which is witnessed (شاهد ومشهود), near the promised day in 85:2. The link to public presence on a day is specific, though the oath's referents are interpreted in more than one way.

The source section's ح-ص-ل root describes collecting a thing, and the section applies it to what is in the breasts; this ayah says that on that day secrets are exposed (تبلى السرائر). It gives a direct parallel for hidden contents brought into view.

The source section expands from a raided crowd to a final gathering; this ayah shows people coming out in separate groups to be shown their deeds (أشتاتا ليروا أعمالهم). It joins collective emergence to individual accounting.

The source section says what is in the breasts is collected for the day; this ayah says whoever has done an atom's weight of good will see it. It gives one side of what the gathering's disclosure makes visible.

The source section says what is in the breasts is collected for the day; this ayah says whoever has done an atom's weight of evil will see it. It supplies the adverse side of the same exact accounting.

The source section's whole-surah context says graves are overturned before the day of collection; this ayah uses the same بعثر wording for when graves are scattered open. It supplies the grave-opening threshold to the gathering.

The source section's whole-surah context asks what is in graves and hearts; this ayah says the earth casts out what is within it and empties itself. It pictures buried contents released before the final assembly.
The source section's gathering day follows the overturning of graves; this ayah says the earth throws out its burdens. It gives the buried multitude's emergence a vivid counterpart.

The source section moves from a crowd held together in the raid to the day of assembly; this ayah pictures people emerging from graves like scattered locusts (جراد منتشر). The dispersed swarm is a specific counter-image to the gathered crowd.

The source section's horses rush into a crowd, and its final scene gathers all people; following the scattered emergence in 54:7, this ayah says they hasten toward the caller. It completes the image of dispersed people moving together toward summons.

The source section's first scene is horses racing into a crowd, later scaled to the final gathering; this ayah shows people rushing from graves as if racing to a marker. The image transfers the section's urgent motion from warhorses to resurrected people.

The source section's جمع image concentrates a crowd; this ayah says that on the Day people will be like scattered moths (الفراش المبثوث). It marks the day’s initial human multitude as dispersal rather than an orderly gathering.

The source section links a small crowd to the day everyone is gathered; this ayah says that when the trumpet is blown, family ties will not connect people and they will not ask one another. It sets a boundary on the tribal relations that make a local crowd a community.

The source section's root ج-م-ع opens a local human crowd toward the final gathering; this ayah says that wherever people are, God will bring them all together (جميعا). It makes the assembly universal across places.

The source section moves from a crowded human group to the day of gathering; this ayah says God will gather the hypocrites and disbelievers together in Hell (جامع المنافقين والكافرين). It gives the assembly a specifically punitive destination.

The source section says what is in the breasts is collected for the day; after 10:28 gathers everyone, this ayah says each soul is tested for what it did and returned to God, its true Lord. It supplies the individual's reckoning within the gathered scene.

The source section connects the gathering day with the witness-root ش-ه-د; this ayah says that on the day a witness is raised from every community. It shows the gathered multitude represented community by community.

The source section joins the جمع crowd to the witness-root ش-ه-د; this ayah says a witness is brought from every community and the Messenger is brought as witness over his people. It makes communal witnessing part of the assembly's judgment.

The source section's root ج-م-ع names a mass of people, and its local scene is a military incursion; this ayah says Pharaoh sends gatherers into the cities to assemble his force. It shows a ruler deliberately collecting a crowd for confrontation.

The source section's جَمْع image is a human crowd met by an approaching force; this ayah describes the two groups coming into sight of each other (تراءى الجمعان) as Moses' people face Pharaoh's force. It supplies a direct encounter between assembled crowds.

The source section scales a small crowd up to the final gathering; this ayah commands that the wrongdoers, their counterparts, and what they worshipped be gathered and led to Hell. It specifies a judgment assembly grouped by its participants and deeds.

The source section brings the human crowd toward a day of gathering before its Lord; this ayah says people will dispute before their Lord on Resurrection Day. It adds open argument to the assembly's reckoning.

The source section's witness-root ش-ه-د and final gathering meet here: on that day the prophets and witnesses are brought, the record is set down, and judgment is made in truth. It specifies testimony and records within the assembled judgment.

The source section says what is in the breasts is collected for the day; after 39:69's public record and judgment, this ayah says every soul is repaid in full for what it did. It states the individual's outcome in that scene.

The source section says what lies in the breasts is collected on the final day; this ayah describes people as exposed before God with nothing hidden from Him. It states the exposure of what had been concealed.

The source section joins hidden contents to the day of account; after 40:16 exposes everyone, this ayah says each soul is repaid for what it earned and no injustice is done. It completes the exposure with its consequence.

The source section says the root ش-ه-د can name a gathering place and being present; this ayah names the day when the witnesses stand (يوم يقوم الأشهاد). It makes witnessing a public event of the final day.

The source section moves from a local human group to the final day; this ayah says that close friends become enemies to one another on that day, except the God-fearing. It marks how earthly group bonds can reverse when the assembly's true affiliations appear.

The source section says what lies in the breasts is collected; this ayah asks whether people with sickness in their hearts think God will not bring out their rancor (أضغانهم). It names a specific hidden content that becomes exposed.

The source section's final gathering is linked to the trumpet; this ayah says the trumpet is blown and calls the moment the promised day. It gives the summons immediately preceding the individual procession in 50:21.

The source section says the witness-root ش-ه-د involves presence at the gathering; following the trumpet in 50:20, this ayah says every soul comes with a driver and a witness (سائق وشهيد). It makes each person's presence and testimony explicit.

The source section says what is hidden in the breasts is collected; after each soul arrives with a witness in 50:21, this ayah says the covering is removed and sight is sharp. It completes the arrival with the removal of concealment.

The source section moves from a people gathered as a local community to the last day; this ayah says relatives and children will not benefit people on Resurrection Day, when God judges between them. It marks the limit of kinship as support in the final assembly.

The source section says what is in the breasts is collected and names 64:9 as the Day of Gathering; this ayah says God knows what people conceal and what they declare, and what is in breasts. It connects the gathering day in this surah with prior knowledge of the inner contents.

The source section pictures everyone collected on the final day; this ayah says people come to God individually (فرادى), stripped of what they had been given. It marks that universal assembly does not erase each person's solitary accounting.
The source section expands one crowd to humanity's final gathering; this ayah says every person comes to the Merciful individually (فردا). It marks the personal arrival within the universal day.

The source section's gathering day brings people before their Lord; after 18:47 gathers everyone and 18:48 presents them in rows, this ayah places the record and says it leaves nothing small or great uncounted. It supplies the detailed account confronting the assembly.

The source section links the gathering day to the witness-root ش-ه-د; this ayah says God will judge among the several religious communities on Resurrection Day and is witness over all things. It brings communities and divine witness into the same judgment scene.

The source section's root ش-ه-د names being present and bearing witness; this ayah has the descendants of Adam testify to God's lordship (شهدنا). It offers a collective witness-scene that contrasts with the final gathering: humanity's testimony begins before its worldly life.

The source section turns a small attacked crowd into humanity assembled on the final day; this ayah says a person flees from his brother. It begins a specific reversal in which the local ties of a crowd no longer hold.

The source section's local crowd is bound as a community; continuing the fleeing scene from 80:34, this ayah names a person's mother and father as those fled from. It extends the day-of-gathering reversal to the closest generational ties.

The source section moves from a local people to the universal day; continuing 80:34-35, this ayah names the spouse and children from whom a person flees. It extends the reversal from parentage to one's household.

The source section's gathering day brings everyone together; after 80:34-36 lists those a person flees, this ayah says each person has a concern that occupies him. It explains the individual urgency within the mass scene.

The source section pictures people gathered on a great day; this ayah shows the Spirit and angels standing in rows, with speech permitted only by the Merciful. It adds an ordered assembly and its limit on speech.

The source section scales a small crowd into the gathering of all people; this ayah names the day mankind stands before the Lord of the worlds. It states the universal assembly as a scene of standing before God.

The source section's root ج-م-ع names people collected for a day; this ayah calls the Day of Decision the appointed time for all together (أجمعين). It makes the day a common appointment for the whole multitude.

The source section says the witness-root ش-ه-د bears on a person's knowledge of his own conduct; this ayah tells each person to read the record, with himself sufficient as reckoner. It makes self-accounting a specific counterpart to the person's testimony.
The source section says what is in the breasts is collected for that day; this ayah says a person will be told what he sent ahead and left behind. It specifies what the day brings back into view.

The source section cites 45:28's gathered communities called to their records; this next ayah says those who believed and did good are admitted by their Lord into mercy. It gives one destination of the assembled communities.

The source section cites 45:28's universal summons to community records; this next ayah addresses the disbelievers and recalls that they acted arrogantly and were criminals. It gives the opposing outcome and the conduct it answers.

The source section explains the root ش-ه-د through witnessing and being present; this ayah says Jesus will be a witness over the People of the Book on Resurrection Day. It places a witness over a community in the final accounting.

The source section's whole-surah context includes the graves being overturned before the day; after people stream from graves in 36:51, this ayah records their question about who raised them from their resting place and the answer that the Merciful's promise is true. It completes the emergence scene with recognition of the summons.

The source section says the final day gathers people and exposes what is inside; this ayah says each soul comes pleading for itself and is repaid in full. It specifies the individual claim and recompense within the multitude.

The source section says what is in the breasts is collected on the day; this ayah says each soul will find the good and evil it did present before it. It gives a concrete disclosure of each person's record.
The source section moves from a local crowd to the great gathering day; this ayah says no close friend will ask another about his state. It marks the failure of social bonds amid the day’s assembly.

The source section takes a human crowd toward a universal day of accounting; this ayah says no soul can avail another on that day and that command belongs to God. It marks the boundary between being gathered together and being able to help one another.

The source section's root ج-م-ع names a human group and places horses amid it; this ayah tells the magicians to gather their plan and come in a row for their contest. It offers a specific, worldly gathering into formation before a confrontation.

The source section turns a human crowd toward the final gathering; this ayah says that on Resurrection Day people will disavow one another and curse the bonds they formed around idols. It shows a group's worldly attachments reversing at the day of account.
